baseline:
B
A standard transformer block is composed of two primary sub-layers: a multi-head self-attention mechanism, which processes the input sequence, followed by a position-wise feed-forward network (which is a type of MLP) that further processes each position independently.

B
An MLP is characterized by its architecture, which includes an input layer, an output layer, and one or more hidden layers. The neurons in these hidden layers use non-linear activation functions (like ReLU or sigmoid) to enable the network to learn complex patterns that are not linearly separable.

B
The MLP (Feed-Forward Network) takes the context-aware vectors produced by the attention layer and applies a non-linear transformation to further process and refine the information for each token.

C
The MLP (feed-forward network) in a transformer block learns to store factual information by adjusting its weights during training. This allows it to associate specific input patterns (keys) with corresponding output patterns (values), effectively acting as a key-value or associative memory.

C
The weights (W) and biases (b) are the parameters that are adjusted during the training process. This tuning encodes the learned patterns from the data, which is how the network stores and recalls information.
